inc-bot: INCIDENT detected: elevated error rate and garbled outputs from hosted runtime (kv-cache reuse suspected). paging @oncall 
raj: oncall here, looking now. can someone dump recent deploys/logs? :mag_right:
mia: I'll take it. I'm on my way, grabbing pod logs and tracing. 
raj: handing over to @mia. set priority P0. customer-facing incidents channel created. :rotating_light:
mia: confirmed -- sudden spike in decode errors and token mismatches on several gen endpoints. Metric: `kv_cache_miss_ratio` jumped from 2% -> 48% in ~3m. Also seeing `wrong_seq_offset` errors in runtime logs.
lars: I think I saw a similar pattern in local repro yesterday when enabling reuse across batch boundaries. Could be reuse correctness.
elaine: customer report: org acme-edge saw repeated invalid completions (merged tokens from previous requests). They rate-limited and rolled back but still got some bad outputs. Customer impact: medium (data leakage risk) — temporarily throttling their traffic.
mia: quick mitigation proposal: disable KV cache reuse and disable continuous batching for hosted pool while we triage. That should stop cross-request leakage. Can we hotfix flags?
raj: approved. do it. get a deploy-ticket and notify customers.
tina: putting templated notif: "We've detected an issue affecting some generations; mitigation in progress, apologies". sending in 5.
deploy-bot: submitted release rollback job #rel-6423 to set `kv_cache_reuse=false` on pool=hosted-gen and `continuous_batching=false`. applying to 4 nodepools canary-first.
mia: executing hotfix now: 
```bash
# patch runtime config for hosted pool
kubectl -n runtime set env ds/runtime-serving KV_CACHE_REUSE=false CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=false --record
```
mia: canary patch applied to 1/4 pods. monitoring canary logs.
deploy-bot: canary succeeded, moving to 2/4.
elaine: temporary guard: add request-level seq-offset verification so if seq requested < cached.seq we reject reuse. can we do a config-level guard quickly?
lars: I can add a runtime flag but it's a code change. quicker is to disable reuse entirely until fix.
mia: canary reached 4/4. error rate dropped ~90% post-hotfix. KV leak traces stopped in canary. rolling to remaining nodes.
raj: nice. start telling impacted customers. include ETA for full rollback completion.
tina: sent customer notif to top 10 impacted orgs, included workaround and timeline.
elaine: rolling restart of serving pods started to flush bad caches. doing one-at-a-time to keep capacity.
mia: during triage found logs with pattern: `reuse_cache: key=<model>:<seq_offset=1234> returns value for seq_offset=1200` — seq offsets mismatch due to stale entries not evicted after batch-splitting. appears when continuous batching splits large requests into sub-batches then reassembles.
lars: root cause hypothesis: reuse lookup keyed only by model+prefix hash, missing seq_offset/req_id in key. when two requests with similar prefixes land close in time, reuse returns wrong KV slice. 
raj: that's consistent with the garbled merged tokens. risk: cross-request leakage of context. escalate to sec if any PII suspected.
elaine: customers reported small snippets of previous conversation leaking; no credentials reported so far. still treat as data leakage risk.
mia: plan for next 6h: 1) keep KV reuse disabled and continuous batching off in hosted. 2) revert any config that might re-enable automatically. 3) rollback code change to add seq_offset into reuse key and add unit+integration tests. 4) add runtime invariant assert to reject mismatched seq offsets with metrics+alerting.
lars: I'll prepare PR for key fix and tests. will target a simple safe change on `reuse_key = model + prefix_hash + seq_offset` and add test for cross-request scenario.
deploy-bot: hotfix fully rolled out to 12/12 pods at 1812004000. incident metric: error_rate down to baseline at 1812004100.
tina: updated customers: "Hotfix applied, we disabled feature X while we fix. No evidence of credential leakage. We'll follow up with root-cause and timeline." 
raj: handing triage to eng-runtime (lars+elaine) for root-cause + postmortem. Oncall remains until at least next update.
mia: creating a runbook entry for this class: "kv-cache reuse correctness" with mitigation steps (disable reuse, disable continuous batching, rolling restart).
elaine: immediate post-incident actions: create regression test harness that simulates batched interleaved requests, add deterministic fuzz of seq offsets. Also correlate logs to find exact customer request pairs that leaked for notification granularity.
lars: PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4271 (fix reuse key + tests). request review from @elaine and @mia. CI includes stress tests.
mia: QA note: need a canary run with replay of captured failing traces before enabling reuse in prod. do not re-enable globally without A/B test.
raj: agreed. we'll also add an alert if `kv_reuse_hits` correlates with `seq_offset_mismatch_count` > 0 for safety.
tina: adding postmortem owners: lars (engineer), mia (sre), elaine (product). ETA first draft in 48h.
elaine: filing incident ticket INC-2026 in tracker with timeline and mitigation steps. link posted.
mia: final status: mitigation in prod, customer notifications sent, oncall handing off to day shift, monitoring for regressions. closing P0 to P1 but keeping incident open for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
raj: thanks team. big thumbs up for quick hotfix + careful canary. remember to scrub any logs before sharing externally.
inc-bot: INCIDENT update: status=mitigated, severity=P1, owner=eng-runtime, incident_ts=1812003456, resolved_ts=1812004100
